plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This holds because your payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks overpaying and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With a value of $46, I should bid exactly $46 to maximize expected profit, as this ensures I win whenever profitable and pay only the second-highest bid, which is always less than or equal to my value when I win.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value ensures I only win when it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With value $17, I'll bid exactly $17.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $28, bidding exactly $28 maximizes my expected profit by ensuring I win whenever it's profitable and never overpay.
